solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Journalist travelled up to collect it

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rode is the past tense of ride, so travelled on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A reporter goes up somewhere to pick something up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the ride word bottom to top before 'collect' takes in the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist who prepares and oversees newspaper copy.

clue.text: A clear soup, right, should be taken in one of our warmer months?

indicators.note: the phrase says one piece is to be enclosed by the other

parts.note: June is a summer month in the northern hemisphere
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a clear broth should be served in a hot summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like the abbreviation R, but here it is LIEN, a legal right over another's goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Julienne is a consommé, a clear broth garnished with thin strips of vegetable.

parts.note: black is used of an ill-omened day, as in a black day for the team
a watch is a guard or lookout kept on duty

explanation.surface: An ill-fated sentry serving in an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Watch is a famous Scottish infantry regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Watch is the name of a historic Highland infantry regiment of the British Army.

clue.text: Girl's drinking hot water brought over in dish

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name; with the possessive it gives IRIS plus S
H is the usual abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: brought over means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: wet is used as a verb meaning to water or dampen

explanation.surface: A girl sips hot water that has been carried across in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's' keeps its possessive S as a letter; 'drinking' and 'brought over' each act on the piece beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a dish of mutton, potatoes and onions stewed together.

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
the person in charge at work

explanation.definitionFit: Boss means both an ornamental raised knob and the person who runs a workplace.

clue.text: When one chooses a woven fabric

parts.note: taken as written
twill is a fabric woven with a diagonal ribbed pattern

explanation.surface: Picking a cloth whenever you please.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adverbial phrase: you may do something at a time of your own choosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever one wishes, by free choice.

indicators.note: new signals that the remaining letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the word is used as the letter pool for the anagram
the letters of this word are taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: A dogmatic university lecturer disregarded fresh regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' says the letters D, O, N are dropped from DOCTRINAIRE, leaving CTRIAIRE, which 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards or principles by which things are judged, a sense close to rules.

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: doubt is suspicion or uncertainty
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a Frenchman's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Parisian' points to the French article, a frequent crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting man's jacket worn in Renaissance times.

indicators.note: after says the second piece comes later than the first

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture in a cup competition

explanation.surface: An argument straight after a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row of seats placed above another, as in a theatre.

clue.text: Cock and duck appearing in list

indicators.note: appearing in says one piece is found inside the other

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A male chicken and a duck are named on a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like another bird beside the cock, but it is O, a nil score.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, the cockerel of the farmyard.

parts.note: read literally, people who jerk with spasms; the slang term for keen birders who chase rare sightings

explanation.definitionFit: Keen bird-spotters are given this slang name, which literally describes people who jerk involuntarily.
Shift as a verb means alter, and as a noun means a loose, straight-cut dress.

clue.text: Frenchman and wife make a fresh start

parts.note: René is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: A French man and his spouse begin their lives over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to begin it again or restore it, a resumption.

clue.text: Filth, look, seen in most of plaza

indicators.note: seen in says one piece appears inside the other
most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a plaza is an open public square
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Dirt and rubbish are visible across most of a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' gives the old exclamation meaning behold; 'most of' drops the final letter of the plaza word.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalor is a state of dirt and wretchedness from neglect.

clue.text: Any clue put out about lead in play?

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the other piece
put out means disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the anagram fodder
the van is the front or leading position, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A solver complains about the leading role in a stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a part in the play, but it is the front position, as in vanguard. Uncle Vanya is by Chekhov.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Vanya is a famous drama by Anton Chekhov.

indicators.note: fallen suggests the letters have tumbled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Examining a tree that has come down.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots pine is a conifer native to northern Europe and Scotland.

clue.text: Artist wearing glasses frames swan and snake?

parts.note: someone wearing glasses is spectacled
a cob is a male swan
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter in specs paints a swan alongside a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames' is loose linking: the swan and artist simply follow; the question mark admits the fanciful picture of a bespectacled snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The spectacled cobra is an Indian snake with eye-like markings on its hood.

parts.note: taken as written
a lake is a surplus, as in the EU wine lake

explanation.surface: A dance show runs into its second week, which is overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excess' gives LAKE, a stockpile of surplus produce, like a wine lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's celebrated ballet.

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An oddball nobleman taking part in a theatrical show.
explanation.walkthrough: Betrayal is a play by Harold Pinter; 'play' looks like part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is the title of a well-known stage drama by Harold Pinter.

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned phrase for a scoundrel or rogue
read literally, an evil piece of millinery

explanation.definitionFit: A bad hat is an old British idiom for a rogue, and literally an evil cap.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A presenter's piece about a scaled-down task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims CHORE to CHOR. An anchor is a broadcaster who links a programme's items.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is a presenter who links the parts of a broadcast.

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, meaning the name contains the run of letters

explanation.surface: A note on the Victorian actress Ellen Terry's achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across ellEN TERry. Ellen Terry was a famous Victorian stage actress.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something is to record it, as in a ledger or register.

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers, are the RE
a turn is a go, someone's opportunity in a game

explanation.surface: Army engineers leave and then come home again.
explanation.definitionFit: To return is to come back to a place.

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sum is a total
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people altogether living in a miserable house.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is a squalid, overcrowded house or district.

clue.text: One won't knock you out in your pub

definitions.meaning: an anaesthetic that numbs one part without making you unconscious
the pub nearest your home that you regularly drink in

explanation.definitionFit: A local is both a local anaesthetic, which keeps you awake, and the neighbourhood pub you frequent.
Like as a verb means be fond of, and as an adjective means similar or equivalent.

clue.text: Harshly criticise drag artist's initial role

parts.note: to drag is to pull

indicators.note: initial points to the first letter of the word

parts.note: a part is a role played by an actor

explanation.surface: A drag performer's first stage role gets savaged by the critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag artist' looks like a single phrase, but drag is PULL and artist's only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull apart a piece of work is to criticise it severely.

parts.note: to knock is to strike
on means about, concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A player lashes out over a breach of the rules during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A knock-on is a rugby offence: the ball is fumbled forward.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, a knock-on is an offence where the ball is dropped forward.

clue.text: Thirty-one days, just in one part of capital

parts.note: May is a month with thirty-one days
fair means just or equitable

explanation.surface: A whole month spent fairly in one district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an expensive district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayfair is a wealthy district in the West End of London, the capital.
